title: Live recording at the Jazz Workshop and the hit 'This Here'
summary: The new Cannonball band with Bobby Timmons and Louis Hayes records live in San Francisco, and Timmons's tune becomes a hit.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And uh, and he had Bobby Timmons playing the piano.

Louis Hayes, and we went to this Workshop out there and Bobby Timmons came over there with one of his little ole funny sounding songs and uh, they brought a truck, a recording truck, and we recorded live.

And this band, yeah when we started the band back then, we was hitting 'em man, and everybody was talking about this brand new band, this new band man, people used to come into the Jazz Workshop, man, like we was you know, all in the streets looking in there, man, we were trying to see this band, and everybody's talking to us all this publicity
about this brand new band, you know.
Cannonball, you know, from the Miles Davis band, his band, you know.
And we uh, was hitting it man, we was hitting it pretty good you know, so we decided to uh, to uh, broadcast live from this club, I mean make a record from this club.
So Bobby Timmons had this little funny sounding song he called it, 'Dis Hyer,' you know.
So we played that thing and in the audience was these two Russian musicians, classical musicians.

All of them, you know, all that you know, publicity and stuff, and it happens so this record man, shot off, man, that thing of Bobby Timmons was a big hit man, so there we go. We're on our way now man.
Shoot man, there was no looking back, kind of, and Cannon haven't looked back since, you know.
